Number Animation collects three animated number components for React built with Framer Motion. Animated Number counts up from its previous value to the new one when it scrolls into view. Number Ticker rolls each digit like a slot machine with a staggered entrance, then rolls changed digits immediately on later updates. Digit Swap keeps every character in a fixed slot and rolls only the glyphs that change, which suits prices, codes and masked values.When to use itA landing page stats section should count up to totals such as users, revenue or downloads as it scrolls into view.A live dashboard, price or balance display needs digits that roll to new values without the text jumping in width.A wallet, OTP or account screen swaps between a real value and a masked one, such as a hidden balance, with a short roll.AccessibilityNumber Ticker and Digit Swap render the full value in visually hidden text and hide the rolling digit columns from assistive technology, so screen readers read the real number instead of individual moving digits. All three use tabular figures so the width stays stable. With reduced motion enabled, Animated Number jumps straight to the final value, Number Ticker sets its digits without rolling or blur, and Digit Swap replaces its vertical roll with a short fade.FAQHow do I make an animated counter in React?Install Animated Number and render AnimatedNumber with a value. It counts up over duration seconds when it enters the viewport, and startOnView={false} starts it immediately. Pass format to control how the number is printed.How do I show decimals, currency or thousands separators in the ticker?NumberTicker takes decimals for fraction digits, locale to insert group separators, prefix and suffix for symbols like $ or %, and pad to left-pad with zeros. A custom format function also works on the client.Can I control the roll direction of Digit Swap?Yes. Set direction to up or down, and tune duration and stagger. Use animationKey to replay every glyph even when characters did not change, and suffixLength with suffixClassName to style the last few characters.
